observedFacts: The extracted article describes 495 fruit-fly traps across Junin, including 102 for Mantaro Valley provinces.
It describes trapping and fruit sampling as surveillance methods used to assess infestation boundaries.
limitations: Original publication date is not established; reported trap counts cannot be presented as current.
Surveillance coverage is not an outbreak or a confirmed local infestation.
Trap coordinates were not present in the extraction.
sources.automation: Use only as source-process context until SENASA supplies a dated current inventory or diagnosed detection.

sources.title: Summer 2027 rain risk scenario, based on SENAMHI technical report 09-2026
sources.geographicScope: Department aggregates include Lima and Junin; district/road intersection not resolved.
sources.accessStatus: Official CENEPRED report PDF extracted with Tavily.
observedFacts: For summer 2027, the report tabulates 363 mass-movement critical zones in Lima and 75 in Junin.
It tabulates 302 flood critical points in Lima and 128 in Junin, within national totals of 2,244.
The ANA critical-point layer data span January 2025-August 2026.
limitations: This is a future seasonal risk scenario, not an active warning or observed event.
Department totals are not PE-22 intersections; geometry archives were not retrieved.
sources.automation: Retain department/district-level scenario data as background only and use published geometry before localizing risk.

sources.provider: INDECI / COEN, summarizing SENAMHI and CENEPRED
sources.title: Monitoring of hazards and outlooks, bulletin 290 (17 October 2026, 15:00 Lima)
sources.geographicScope: National bulletin; includes a measured rainfall observation at Ingenio, Concepción, Junín, and forecast-warning summaries affecting Lima and Junín.
sources.accessStatus: Official INDECI PDF extracted successfully with Tavily.
observedFacts: For 16 October 07:00 to 17 October 07:00, the bulletin reports 12.0 mm at Ingenio station, Concepción province, Junín, classified as a rainy day.

It summarizes SENAMHI warning 422 for 18–19 October, including Lima and Junín; the notice forecasts central-Andes precipitation and conditions for hail, high-altitude snow, electrical discharges and strong gusts.
The bulletin also contains nationwide water-storage, temperature and risk-scenario summaries; these are not all local road observations.
limitations: The rainfall value is a station measurement, not rainfall on a road segment; station coordinates are rounded in the available atlas.
Warning 422 is a forecast and its advertised geometry ZIPs could not be extracted; province coverage alone does not establish PE-22 overlap.
The daily bulletin contains multiple hazards and dates; each table must retain its own observation window and notice validity.
sources.automation: Archive the bulletin PDF by publication time; parse observation tables separately from warning tables, retain station/time/classification, and follow published GIS links only after validating the downloaded geometries.

sources.provider: INDECI / COEN, citing Lima regional and Surco district risk offices
sources.title: Complementary report 14162: forest fire and agricultural damage in Ayas, Surco, Huarochirí
sources.geographicScope: Ayas annex, Surco district, Huarochirí province, Lima; exact point and affected-field polygon were not provided.
sources.accessStatus: All six pages of the official COEN PDF extracted with Tavily.
observedFacts: INDECI reports a forest fire at Ayas, Surco, beginning 30 September 2026 at 12:49; the report says it was extinguished and closed.
The damage table, updated 2 October 10:55, records 45 hectares of agricultural crops affected and 25 hectares of natural cover destroyed.
The report lists palta, chirimoya, alfalfa, membrillo, tuna and eucalyptus among affected crops/vegetation; it reports no deaths or injuries.
limitations: This is a completed historical fire, not a current fire alert or a verified road closure.
Damage acreage is district-office reporting while EDAN was being updated; retain the stated update time.
Ayas is named as an annex, but exact incident coordinates and field boundaries are absent; do not geocode to a district centroid.
sources.automation: Ingest report revisions as versions; preserve occurrence date, updated damage date, crop area, closure status and locality separately; keep geometry null until an official point or field boundary is supplied.

sources.title: Summer 2027 rain risk scenario (official update published 7 October 2026)
sources.geographicScope: National Peru; January-March 2027 scenario. No PE-22 intersection computed.
sources.accessStatus: Official press release and study metadata extracted; regional archive geometry was not downloaded.
observedFacts: The release identifies 702 districts at very high risk from mass movements and 8,695,261 inhabitants across those districts.
In areas of greater susceptibility to mass movements, the release reports 3,333,277 residents, 63,290 km of road network and 3,610,747 ha of agricultural area.
The separate flood scenario reports 3,571,687 residents and 7,673 km of road network in areas of greater susceptibility.
limitations: National scenario and exposure totals are not current incidents or PE-22 counts.
Exact corridor exposure requires inspection of the linked official spatial artifacts.
sources.automation: Archive each scenario version and only publish corridor intersections after validating official district or hazard geometry.

sources.title: Water-deficit risk scenario for the 2026-2027 rainy period, September update
sources.geographicScope: National; department-level very-high-risk district counts include Junin and Pasco. No corridor geometry extracted.
sources.accessStatus: Official CENEPRED PDF extracted with Tavily.
observedFacts: The report identifies 397 districts nationally at very high water-deficit risk, including 18 in Junin and 10 in Pasco.
Across all very-high-risk districts, it reports 2,466,388 ha of agricultural land and 8,024,224 ha of pasture.
limitations: This is seasonal risk, not an observed water shortage or current irrigation restriction.
Department-level counts do not identify a PE-22 intersection.
sources.automation: Refresh on official reissue, retain the season/version and require a verified spatial layer before mapping local exposure.

sources.title: Official critical-zone points linked to weather notices
sources.geographicScope: Peru; the retrieved layer contains 303 critical zones in six northern departments linked to SENAMHI notice 421.
sources.accessStatus: 303 GeoJSON point features extracted successfully through Tavily from the official ArcGIS service.
observedFacts: Each point publishes an OBJECTID, hazard, locality, exposed elements, notice number and INGEMMET zone level.
All 303 retrieved points are associated with notice 421; the source classifies 160 as Nivel 2 and 143 as Nivel 3.
limitations: Critical zones under a forecast are not confirmed landslides, damaged assets or road closures.
INGEMMET's NIVEL classification is separate from SENAMHI's warning level; the point-level source value is preserved in the map record.
The layer has no incident-occurrence date; published forecast validity comes from the referenced SENAMHI notice.
Native CLI requests to these domains failed DNS in this environment. This is a documented capture, not an automatically refreshed feed.
sources.automation: Query official GeoJSON and validate the notice association and its validity before replacing the capture. Preserve previous captures and reject missing geometry or unmatched notices.

sources.title: Official daily weather-warning polygons (WFS)
sources.geographicScope: Peru; verified daily risk polygons from notices 415, 420, 421 and 422.
sources.accessStatus: Eight official WFS responses extracted through Tavily; notice IDs, map IDs, issue dates and daily validity verified in feature properties.
observedFacts: The retained 13 risk features form 11 daily warning-area records when equal notice/map/level features are grouped without changing their polygons.
Only Nivel 2 and higher are mapped; Nivel 1 national background polygons are excluded.
Warning 422 day one begins at 19:00 UTC (14:00 Lima) on 18 October 2026.
limitations: Warning geometry is forecast coverage, not an observed event or proof of a road/mining-site impact.
A daily map can have a shorter validity than its parent notice.
No centroid, district pin or invented geometry replaces an official polygon.
sources.automation: Fetch published daily WFS maps, check IDs against requested notice/map/year, validate closed WGS84 rings and source dates, retain risk levels only and evaluate expiry from each map's published validity.
